resolution: Found and fixed the editor↔compiled SCALE mismatch on prop part textures (image small/tiled in the iso editor #14, but full-size in the compiled game #15). Root cause: req_0757's DataProp gave non-panel ('chassis') parts a SIZE-DERIVED capture grid — tex = { cols: skinGridCols(max(w,d)), floors: skinGridFloors(h) }, and skinGridCols = clampInt(width/3,1,10) — so any part bigger than ~3m tiled the image into multiple small copies in the /test editor. The COMPILED path (worldGeometry.pushPropPart) interns the material by texture id with NO grid at all, so the engine samples one whole image per face — the look the user wanted. Fix: every prop part now bakes at a 1x1 grid (one whole image per face), identical to the compiled path; removed the now-unused skinGridCols/skinGridFloors import. Verified by a clean full-graph esbuild pass. Committed fd67ed8d2. SEPARATE ISSUE the user also flagged (#11-13): a prop that is supposed to be GLASS renders wrong after an apply→compile→return-to-editor round-trip — that is a glass-transparency interaction, NOT this scale bug; logged as a distinct follow-up, not fixed here.
